references.text: In the preceding verse, the Lord commands that the mina be taken from the servant who hid it and given to the one who has ten minas. Verse 25 records the bystanders' reaction to this command—they point out that he already has ten minas ([ref:Luk 19:24|Luke 19:24]).

Jesus responds to the objection in verse 25 with the well-known principle: "I tell you, everyone who has will be given more, and from the one who does not have, even what they have will be taken away" ([ref:Luk 19:26|Luke 19:26]).

In the parable of the talents in Matthew, there is a parallel where the Lord commands that the talent be taken from the lazy servant and given to the one who has ten, followed by the same principle that whoever has will receive more ([ref:Matt 25:28-29|Matthew 25:28-29]).

The principle that whoever has will receive more is also stated by Jesus in connection with the parables of the kingdom of God: "For to everyone who has, more will be given, and they will have an abundance" ([ref:Matt 13:12|Matthew 13:12]).
Mark records the same principle: "For whoever has will receive more. And from the one who does not have, even what they have will be taken away" ([ref:Mark 4:25|Mark 4:25]).

Luke also presents this principle earlier in the gospel, in connection with listening to God's word: "Whoever has will receive more, and whoever does not have, even what they think they have will be taken away" ([ref:Luk 8:18|Luke 8:18]).
